summary: This work experimentally demonstrates quantum charging advantage (QCA) in superconducting quantum batteries with 2–12 transmon qubits arranged in a linear chain, using only nearest-neighbor pairwise two-photon interactions. The quantum charging protocol (double-excitation Hamiltonian $V_\mathrm{qu} = \sum_{n=1}^{N-1} \hbar g(\sigma_n^+ \sigma_{n+1}^+ + \sigma_n^- \sigma_{n+1}^-)$) outperforms classical local driving ($V_\mathrm{cl} = \sum_n \hbar \Omega(\sigma_n^+ + \sigma_n^-)$) under equal energy constraints.
motivation: Prior theoretical proposals for QCA required complex many-body or long-range all-to-all interactions; this work addresses the gap between theory and experiment by demonstrating QCA with experimentally accessible nearest-neighbor pairwise couplings in a scalable solid-state platform.
method: Using a 16-qubit superconducting lattice with frequency-tunable couplers, the authors implement parametric bSWAP operations via sinusoidal flux modulation at frequency $\omega_d \approx \omega_n + \omega_{n+1}$ to engineer two-photon transitions. They measure ergotropy, average charging power $\overline{\mathcal{P}}_\mathrm{opt}(N)$, and the advantage parameter $\Gamma_\mathrm{ad} = \overline{\mathcal{P}}^\mathrm{opt}_\mathrm{qu}/\overline{\mathcal{P}}^\mathrm{opt}_\mathrm{cl} - 1$, along with entanglement via second-order Rényi entropy.
result: Quantum charging achieves $\Gamma_\mathrm{ad}(N) > 0$ with $\eta(N) \geq 0$ for $N \in [2,12]$, confirming genuine QCA without excess energy cost; the maximum power scales linearly with $N$ for quantum charging versus sublinear for classical, with measured effective coupling $g \approx 1.03 \times 2\pi$ MHz, coherent and incoherent ergotropy contributions, and $g^{(2)} > 1$ (giant bunching) indicating anti-blockade-like excitation-facilitating dynamics.
